name: Shilshah
title: Ezra's wife who was sent away
summary: Shilshah was one of the foreign women married to Israelite men after the return from exile in Babylon. She is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the women who were sent away during Ezra's reforms to preserve Israel's religious purity.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reform against mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had married foreign women. He implemented a reform to separate from these women and maintain the holiness of the people.

keyEvents.title: The people's confession
keyEvents.description: The people gathered and confessed their sin of taking foreign wives. They committed themselves to sending away the foreign women.

keyEvents.title: The list of those who had taken foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Shilshah is mentioned among the names of those who had married foreign women and were required to separate from them.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's prayer and grief
keyEvents.description: Ezra grieved deeply over the people's unfaithfulness to God through mixed marriages, and he offered a heartfelt prayer for forgiveness on behalf of the people.
